cable.definition: A cable is a strong wire or rope that is often made out of metal.
cable.sentence: A strong cable held the two trees together.

cake.definition: A cake is a sweet baked food.
cake.sentence: Natasha's mum baked her a cake for her birthday.

calculate.definition: If you calculate something, you find its value, usually by using mathematics.
calculate.sentence: The computers can calculate how much your family can afford to pay for college.

call.definition: If you call someone, you contact them using a telephone.
call.sentence: I can't talk now. I'll call back later.

calm.definition: If a person, place or situation is calm, it is peaceful and quiet.
calm.sentence: There's no wind and the lake is calm.

camera.definition: An object that takes pictures digitally or on film.
camera.sentence: I took a picture of the mountain with my camera.

camp.definition: A camp is a place, usually outside of cities, where people stay for a short time.
camp.sentence: I don't think I can walk anymore today. Let's set up camp for the night.

campaign.definition: A campaign is a group of activities working towards a particular goal, often to elect a political candidate or in a war.
campaign.sentence: Angry TV viewers did launch a letter-writing campaign against CBS's decision to cancel the show.

can.definition: If someone can do something, they are able to do it.

cancel.definition: If you cancel something that was going to happen, you decide that it will not happen.
cancel.sentence: I'm afraid I can't make it; I'll have to cancel.

candidate.definition: A candidate is one person or thing that may be chosen, especially in an election.
candidate.sentence: Because the school has a lot of poor children, it's a good candidate to receive extra money.

cap.definition: A cap is a small hat.
cap.sentence: He was wearing blue jeans and a ball cap.

capability.definition: We say that someone has a capability when they are capable of doing something; that means they are able to do it.
capability.sentence: He worked to the limits of his capability.

capable.definition: If someone or something is capable of something, they can do it.
capable.sentence: I'm quite capable of looking after myself and I don't need you to tell me how.

capacity.definition: The capacity of a container, room, etc. is how much it can hold.
capacity.sentence: If you fill it to capacity, you won't be able to carry it.

capital.definition: A capital is the most important city of a country. The government of the country is usually located there.

capture.definition: If you capture a person or animal, you catch them and do not let them go free.

car.definition: A car is a small passenger vehicle with four wheels, moved by an engine.
car.sentence: I just drive around in my car all day.

carbon.definition: The chemical element (symbol C) with an atomic number of 6.
carbon.sentence: Make sure the carbon is facing the second sheet of paper, before rolling it into the typewriter.

card.definition: A card is a small, often rectangular piece of paper or plastic, usually with information.
card.sentence: The police stopped me and asked to see my identity card.

care.definition: Care is the act of helping someone, especially sick people, the very young or the very old.
care.sentence: He decided not to seek health care from a hospitals.

career.definition: A career is a job or a series of related jobs that you do for many years.
career.sentence: She says that she enjoyed making the movie, but has no plans to pursue an acting career.

careful.definition: If you are careful, then you do not take risks and are cautious; you have care.
careful.sentence: Edward had to be very careful when walking with the hot soup bowl in his hands because he could spill it and burn himself.

carefully.definition: When something is done carefully, it is done with caution.
carefully.sentence: Timmy, take that vase out in our room carefully.

carpet.definition: A carpet is a floor covering, usually made of nylon or wool.
carpet.sentence: He walked in with his boots leaving snow on the carpet.

carry.definition: If you carry something, you lift it up and move it to another place.
carry.sentence: Let me carry those bags in for you.

case.definition: A case is a container to hold something.
case.sentence: He opened the case and pulled out his violin.

cash.definition: Cash is money in the form of bills and coins, rather than checks/cheques or credit cards.
cash.sentence: The publisher supplied cash prizes and books for the winning essays written by fourth through sixth graders.

cast.definition: If x casts light or shadow on y, x causes y to be lit or in shadow.
cast.sentence: The street light outside my window cast shadows on the wall.

castle.definition: A castle is a large, strong building used to protect the people inside.

cat.definition: A cat is a domestic animal often kept as a pet; it has whiskers and likes to chase mice.
cat.sentence: Our pet cat has just had kittens.

catalog.definition: A catalog is a list of items.
catalog.sentence: Look through the catalog to find the book you're looking for.

catch.definition: A catch is something that is caught, like the fish a fishermen catches.
catch.sentence: My dad brought home a good catch of trout today.

category.definition: A category is a group of people or things that are the same in some way.

cause.definition: A cause is what leads to something happening.
cause.sentence: The cause of the fire was lightning.

celebrate.definition: If you celebrate something, you do something special to show that you are happy about it.
celebrate.sentence: Some American homes are treeless during Christmas as these families celebrate other holidays.

celebration.definition: A celebration is a gathering of people for fun and entertainment, usually like a party.
celebration.sentence: We held a birthday celebration for Jane last Sunday.

cell.definition: A cell is a room in a jail where prisoners are kept.
cell.sentence: He was arrested and kept in a small cell for one day.

cent.definition: A small coin of little value, also called a penny; 100 cents make a dollar.

center.definition: The center of something, is the place that is as far from its outside as possible.
center.sentence: The president and his problems continue to take center stage in the news.

central.definition: A thing is central when it is in the middle.
central.sentence: The house is central to all of the stores.

century.definition: A century is a period of 100 years.
century.sentence: My great grandfather came to Canada over a century ago.

ceremony.definition: A ceremony is a religious or social event with a number of things that are traditionally done or said.
ceremony.sentence: We are going to get married in a big wedding ceremony.

certain.definition: If you are certain of something, you believe it to be true without doubt.
certain.sentence: Set aside a certain sum each week.

certainly.sentence: She certainly is a hard worker.

chain.definition: A chain is a series of round pieces of material joined together to make a line.
chain.sentence: He got her a gold chain necklace for her birthday.

chair.definition: A chair is a piece of furniture for one person to sit on.
chair.sentence: Please, pull up a chair and sit down.

chairman.definition: A chairman is the person who controls a meeting or an organization.
chairman.sentence: Alan Eastwood is the former chairman of the Police Federation.

challenge.definition: A challenge is something difficult that you want or have to do.
challenge.sentence: Many churches overseas are struggling to meet the AIDS challenge.

chamber.definition: A chamber is a room that is often used for sleeping.
chamber.sentence: He went to his chamber to get some rest.

champion.definition: A champion is someone who has been a winner in a contest.
champion.sentence: I was the race and so now I am this year's champion.

championship.definition: A championship is a contest to decide which person or team is best at the sport.
championship.sentence: Gene Tunney won the world heavyweight boxing championship from Jack Dempsey.

change.definition: If you change something, you make it different than before.
change.sentence: Change before you go to the opera.

channel.definition: A channel is a path that carries or directs flow or movement, especially of TV & radio signals and water.
channel.sentence: We have to keep our boat in the channel.

chapter.definition: A chapter is a main division of a book.
chapter.sentence: We read chapter five in the blue textbook.

character.definition: Someone's character is the combination of things that they do, feel, and believe that makes them a certain type of person.
character.sentence: He's got a really funny character.

characteristic.definition: A characteristic of something is a typical feature.
characteristic.sentence: Good hearing is one characteristic of dogs.

characterize.definition: To see someone or something a particular way (often negative).
characterize.sentence: You can characterize his behavior as that of an egotist.

charge.definition: When you charge someone money, you ask them to pay the money for something that you have done for them or sold to them.
charge.sentence: We charge ten cents a page for copying.

charity.definition: A charity is an organisation that collects money or goods and uses them to help poor or sick people, often with the help of volunteers.
charity.sentence: All the money raised goes to charity.

charm.definition: A charm is an object that people think has a magical power.
charm.sentence: His old pencil was a charm for him. He always used it on tests.

chart.definition: A chart is information that is organised in rows and columns or as a picture.
chart.sentence: This week's bar chart shows the correct figures.

chase.definition: If you chase something, you go after it quickly.
chase.sentence: He waved his arms to chase the birds out of the cherry tree.

chat.definition: If two or more people chat, they talk with each other in a casual way, sometimes by typing on a computer or cell phone.
chat.sentence: His friends dropped by frequently just to chat.

cheap.definition: If something is cheap, it costs very little money.
cheap.sentence: I don't like that jacket. It looks too cheap. Is it plastic?

check.definition: If you check something, you look at it to see if there is a problem, or something new or different.
check.sentence: Can you check that the lights are off?

cheek.definition: The soft skin on each side of the face, below the eyes.
cheek.sentence: You’ve got some cheek, asking me for money!

cheese.definition: Cheese is a food that is made by mixing bacteria with milk and aging it.
cheese.sentence: I often eat cheese with bread and grapes.

chemical.definition: A chemical is a basic substance that is used in or produced by mixing elements or other chemicals.
chemical.sentence: The chemical industry in China is producing more and more useful paints, glues, and other products.

chest.definition: A type of box with a lid that you can lock.
chest.sentence: He put his things in the chest.

chicken.definition: A chicken is a bird that farmers raise for meat and eggs.
chicken.sentence: My father went out back, caught a chicken, cut off its head, and cleaned it for dinner.

chief.definition: A leader or respected elder in a tribe.
chief.sentence: They came to the chief to resolve their dispute.

child.definition: A child is a young person, usually older than a baby but younger than a teenager.
child.sentence: Even as a child of six, I knew what hard work was.

childhood.definition: Childhood is the state or condition of being an child, that is, being under 18 years of age.
childhood.sentence: Childhood is the first stage of every man's life.

chip.definition: A small piece that is broken off of a larger object.
chip.sentence: A chip of paint fell off the wall.

chocolate.definition: Chocolate is a candy made from cacao beans and often used to flavour other foods such as cakes and cookies.
chocolate.sentence: In my opinion, the best cookies are those that contain chocolate.

choice.definition: If you have a choice, you can decide between two or more things or actions.
choice.sentence: I don't want to go, but I'm afraid I don't have a choice.

choose.definition: When you choose a thing, you decide you want it and not something else.
choose.sentence: The manager and coaches will choose the starting line-up.

church.definition: The Church is Christians gathering to praise and be with God.
church.sentence: Though she prayed and attended church, as she got older she often wondered why God didn't do anything.

circle.definition: A circle (●) is a round shape.
circle.sentence: Please put your chairs in a circle.

circumstance.definition: The circumstances surrounding an action or event includes all the information that helps you understand the action or event.
circumstance.sentence: We hadn't planned it, but we ended up together by circumstance.

cite.definition: If you cite people or facts, you write or talk about them to support your point or show where you got your information.

citizen.definition: A citizen is a person who lives in a particular place.

city.definition: A city is large area where many people live and work, larger than a town.
city.sentence: There's too much crime in this city.

civil.definition: About the citizens of a country, especially as opposed to the government, army, police, religion, etc.
civil.sentence: One of the most important civil rights is freedom of speech.

civilian.definition: A civilian is a person who is not in the country's army.
civilian.sentence: Its against the law for a soldier to hurt a civilian.

claim.definition: If you claim something, you say or write that it is true without proof.
claim.sentence: It is easy to claim that a god exists, but impossible to prove.

class.definition: A class is a time for learning.

classic.definition: If something is classic, it's typical.
classic.sentence: Richard Branson is a classic example of success without schooling.

classical.definition: Classical ideas or styles are those that were very common at a time in the past and sometimes continue into the present.
classical.sentence: Classical theories in physics can't explain certain observations, which has led scientists to come up with new theories.

clause.definition: A clause is a section in a contract or other legal document.
clause.sentence: The author's contract contained a clause giving him creative control over the films.

clean.definition: If something is clean, it is free from dirt.
clean.sentence: The kids came back from the washroom with clean hands and faces.

clear.definition: A clear idea is an idea that is easy to understand.
clear.sentence: OK, so you need the key. I see. That's clear now.

clearly.definition: If something is clearly true, then it is easy to see that it is true.
clearly.sentence: The building is clearly visible from the air.

click.definition: Click is the act of operating a switch so that it clicks.
click.sentence: A click on the right button for example.

climate.definition: The weather conditions of a place.
climate.sentence: The desert is a very hot climate to be in.

climb.definition: If you climb something, you move up or down it.
climb.sentence: Narrow steps climb to the door of a small temple.

clinical.definition: Clinical work or practice is related to the observation and treatment of patients.
clinical.sentence: She is doing her clinical training at the hospital.

clock.definition: If a clock is fast, it shows a time after the real time.
clock.sentence: The digital clock on the wall tells her that it is almost six-thirty.

close.definition: If you close something, you change it from being open to not open.
close.sentence: Sadly, we have decided to close the shop.

closely.definition: If something is closely related, linked, or involved it is strongly so.
closely.sentence: The birds on this island are closely related to those on the mainland.

clothes.definition: Clothes, such as shirts, pants, socks, etc. are things that people wear on their body to cover it.
clothes.sentence: He took off his clothes and got into the shower.

clothing.definition: When you speak of clothes in general, you speak of clothing.
clothing.sentence: Shoes, shirts, and trousers are types of clothing.

cloud.definition: A cloud is a collection of condensed water vapor floating in the sky that sometimes makes rain.
cloud.sentence: The cloud of locusts flew closer to the corn.

club.definition: A club is an organisation of people who share a similar sport, interest, or hobby.
club.sentence: He was a member of his high school drama club.

cluster.definition: A cluster is anything that is more than one thing put together.
cluster.sentence: In the market, you can find a cluster of bananas.

coach.definition: A coach is a teacher of a sport.
coach.sentence: Even though his team won, first-year coach Andrew Johnson was not happy.

coal.definition: Coal is a fuel which comes from under the ground. It is black, or sometimes brown. People often burn it for heat.

coast.definition: The coast is the area of land closest to the sea.
coast.sentence: The hotel was near the coast and their room had a balcony from which they could see the distant ocean.

coat.definition: An outer piece of clothing that covers the upper part of the body and the arms.
coat.sentence: The woman wore a fur coat.

code.definition: A code is a set of rules or laws.
code.sentence: Children usually learn their parents' moral code.

coffee.definition: Coffee is a dark brown drink that is very popular around the world.
coffee.sentence: Would you like a cup coffee or tea?

coin.definition: A coin is money made of metal.

cold.definition: If something is cold, it is low in temperature.
cold.sentence: The wind made her hands cold.

collapse.sentence: The collapse of the bridge means we can't go over the river any longer.

colleague.definition: A colleague is a person who works together with another person or who does the same kind of work.

collect.definition: If you collect some things, you bring them together as a group.

collection.definition: A collection is a group of things of the same type. They are usually special in some way.
collection.sentence: The school took a collection for new books.

college.definition: A college is a school for adults who have finished high school.
college.sentence: I went to the college of medicine at the University of Wales.

color.definition: The image caused by light in your eyes, due to light of various wavelengths hitting your retina.

column.definition: A column is a support that is standing up and is built to support something, usually on a building.
column.sentence: He added a column of numbers.

combination.definition: A combination is an item or group made of different things or kinds of things.
combination.sentence: Any combination of these factors increases the risk dramatically.

combine.definition: If you combine two or more things, you put them together.
combine.sentence: All of these factors combine to create a system that is difficult to understand.

come.definition: To move towards a place or into a place; to move to the place where the person who is talking is.
come.sentence: Come to my house and I will give you something to eat.

comedy.definition: A comedy is a humorous drama.

comfort.definition: Comfort is a feeling in your body that there are no problems.
comfort.sentence: Enjoying the comfort of his own bed, he soon fell asleep.

comfortable.definition: If a piece of furniture, clothing, a room, etc. is comfortable, you feel comfortable in it (see 2.)
comfortable.sentence: There were a few old but comfortable chairs in the meeting area.

command.definition: Command, is the power to control people or things.
command.sentence: The information moved from the soldiers up the chain of command right to the president.

comment.definition: A comment is a short statement about something; usually it is an opinion.
comment.sentence: I'm afraid I can't make any comment on the case right now.

commercial.definition: If something is commercial, it is related to buying, selling, trading and money.
commercial.sentence: Education is much more difficult than many industrial and commercial processes to measure.

commission.definition: A commission is a group of people who work together to research or manage something for a government.
commission.sentence: She was recently appointed to head the European commission on climate change.

commit.definition: If you commit something illegal or bad, you do it.
commit.sentence: We must commit ourselves to the job at hand.

commitment.definition: A commitment is a formal promise or agreement.
commitment.sentence: You don't have to make a firm commitment but we would like to know when you can probably start work.

committee.definition: A group of people that come together to do something or decide something.
committee.sentence: He is on the administrative committee. They decide how to administer the school.

common.definition: Mutual; shared by more than one.
common.sentence: The two teams have the common goal of winning the game.

communicate.definition: If you communicate an idea, you make someone else understand your idea, usually by using words.
communicate.sentence: Parents have to work hard to communicate better with their children.

communication.definition: Communication is the process of sending and receiving ideas between two or more people.
communication.sentence: Teachers must regularly practice their communication skills to make sure students understand them easily.

community.definition: A community is a group of people living in the same area and having a similar background or similar interests.
community.sentence: Most Libyan policemen were members of the community where they worked.

company.definition: A company is an organization for doing work for money.
company.sentence: He works for a big company.

compare.definition: If you compare two things, you look at, talk about, or think about how they are the same and how they are different.
compare.sentence: This car does not compare with our line of Mercedes.

comparison.definition: When someone makes a comparison between two things, the person thinks about how the two things are the same and how they are different, which one is bigger etc.
comparison.sentence: A careful comparison will show that this cup has a little more water than the other cup.

compensation.definition: Compensation is money, or something of value, given to somebody who has lost something or been harmed.
compensation.sentence: They are asking for compensation for the damage to their car.

compete.definition: If you compete for something, you are working against other people to get it.
compete.sentence: Is it a good idea to allow female athletes to compete in male high school athletic events?

competition.definition: Competition is a situation or event in which people or groups try to succeed over each other.
competition.sentence: With increasing international competition, companies are cutting costs to survive.

competitive.definition: If someone is competitive, they want very much to be the best at everything.
competitive.sentence: I don't enjoy working with her because she's so competitive.

competitor.definition: A competitor is someone who is competing in a race or an event.

complain.definition: If you complain about someone or something, you say or write that you are not happy about it.

complaint.definition: A complaint is an expression of dissatisfaction.
complaint.sentence: He had a skin complaint and so went to the doctor for advice.

complete.definition: To finish; to reach the end.
complete.sentence: A child would complete the family.

completely.definition: When something is completely some quality, it is absolutely that quality, in every way.
completely.sentence: The man was completely honest in his business.

complex.definition: If something is complex, it has lots of parts or pieces, or is difficult to understand.
complex.sentence: He has constructed a complex computer system to send translated messages between humans and dolphins.

complexity.definition: Complexity is the state of something being complex.
complexity.sentence: He enjoyed the complexity of modern computers.

complicate.definition: If you complicate a task, you make it difficult to do.
complicate.sentence: Just tell me the facts. Please don't complicate the account with unnecessary details.

component.definition: A component is one part that connects to other parts.
component.sentence: The main component of any budget will be the cost of staff.

compose.definition: If you compose something, then you create or write it.
compose.sentence: He decided to compose a symphony.

composition.definition: The parts that make up something.
composition.sentence: Harmonious composition is essential in a serious work of art.

compound.definition: A compound is a material made of a number of other materials.
compound.sentence: The new chemical compound has far less smell than the original substance.

comprehensive.definition: If something is comprehensive, it includes everything that is related.
comprehensive.sentence: The book includes the most comprehensive list of existing government programs.

comprise.definition: If x comprises y, y is part of x.
comprise.sentence: Fifty states comprise The United States.

compromise.definition: A compromise is an agreement in which everyone gets only some of what they wanted.
compromise.sentence: The two parties who were arguing came to a compromise.

compute.definition: If you compute an answer, you calculate it or find it, usually using mathematics.

computer.definition: A computer is a machine that helps you store, organize, and use information.
computer.sentence: If you're looking at a web page, you must be using a computer.

concentrate.definition: If you concentrate on something, you use most of your time and work there.
concentrate.sentence: I went to a quiet room so I could concentrate.

concentration.definition: A concentration is a large amount of something in one place or group.
concentration.sentence: The growing concentration of people in cities is causing new problems.

concern.definition: A concern about something means something that a person is worried about.
concern.sentence: The government expressed its concern at the fighting in Kenya.

concert.definition: A concert is a musical performance, usually of several selections.
concert.sentence: The concert included a Mozart serenade and a Tchaikovsky symphony.

conclude.definition: When something concludes, you come to an end of it.
conclude.sentence: After living in this city for some time, I conclude that the people here are quite warm and friendly.

conclusion.definition: A writer or speaker's conclusions are the ideas that they have after thinking about all the important information.
conclusion.sentence: The study's main conclusion is that more money will not solve the problem.

concrete.definition: Concrete is a type of mix that, when dried, hardens, often for sidewalks.
concrete.sentence: Did you know that the sidewalk was made out of concrete?

condition.definition: A condition is a logical clause or phrase that a conditional statement uses. The phrase can either be true or false.
condition.sentence: The doctor will check my condition.

conduct.definition: If you conduct an activity or process, you do it or carry it out.
conduct.sentence: The war made it very difficult to conduct business.

conference.definition: A conference is a large organised meeting to discuss a particular topic or area.
conference.sentence: Contact the teacher or coach and ask for a private conference without your child's presence.

confidence.definition: Confidence is the state of trusting something, and being sure that something is going to happen.
confidence.sentence: I know you're trying to gain confidence in what you're doing.

confident.definition: When someone is confident, the person is certain of something.
confident.sentence: I am confident that I will win.

confirm.definition: If something confirms an idea, it show that it is true.
confirm.sentence: The results of the study confirm previous research on the topic.

conflict.definition: A conflict is when two or more people or ideas don't agree.
conflict.sentence: The two stories examine the conflict between good and evil.

confuse.definition: If you confuse someone, they don't understand what you have said or done.
confuse.sentence: Try not to confuse accept with except.

confusion.definition: Confusion is a feeling you get when things are unclear or you don't understand.
confusion.sentence: The snow storm caused great confusion at the airport where many planes were unable to take off or land.

connect.definition: When you connect things, you join, link or unite them.
connect.sentence: Can you connect the two loudspeakers?

connection.definition: A connection is a way that two or more things come or belong together.
connection.sentence: Who was the first person to make the connection between sickness and cleanliness?

consequence.definition: A consequence is a result of an action, decision, etc., often a bad result.
consequence.sentence: As a consequence of your bad behavior, you must stay after school.

consequently.definition: The word consequently is used show what happened as a result or consequence of an event.
consequently.sentence: He did not wake up early in the morning. Consequently, he was late to work.

conservative.definition: If a person is conservative, they do not like change.
conservative.sentence: Latino families are thought to hold conservative and traditional views on family life.

consider.definition: When you consider something you think carefully about it.
consider.sentence: I will take time to consider what you said.

considerable.definition: A considerable amount, time, degree, etc. is a fairly large or important one.
considerable.sentence: He had given it a considerable amount of thought before deciding.

consideration.definition: Consideration is the process of thinking carefully about something.
consideration.sentence: After much consideration, I think I will retire.

consist.definition: If A consists of B, then B is the thing or things that, together, make A.

consistent.definition: If something is consistent, it is regular and you can guess what it will be like in the future.
consistent.sentence: She makes a consistent effort to study hard.

constant.definition: If something is constant, it doesn't change over time.
constant.sentence: I have this constant pain in my back. I wish it would stop.

constantly.definition: Constantly means continuously over a period of time; always.

constitute.definition: If something is being constituted, it is being set up or established.
constitute.sentence: Truth and reason constitute the intellectual gold that defies destruction.

constraint.sentence: Perhaps the main constraint is lack of money.

construct.sentence: That artwork is a construct of wires and tubes.

construction.definition: Construction is the act of building something.
construction.sentence: The workers began construction of the new hospital last week.

consult.sentence: I have a consult with a sleep specialist this afternoon.

consultant.definition: A consultant is a person who is consulted by another person, a company, a government, or other kind of entity, especially for legal or business purposes.
consultant.sentence: The district hired a consultant to help write the letter to parents.

consume.definition: If you consume energy, resources, time, etc., you use it and it is no longer available.
consume.sentence: Many people do not consume adequate amounts of food for good health.

consumer.definition: A consumer is someone who buys or uses goods or services.
consumer.sentence: Consumer demand for large cars has dropped with the increase in gasoline prices.

contact.definition: When x makes or has contact with y, they touch each other physically.
contact.sentence: The trains in Tokyo are so crowded that everyone has to stand in close contact to everyone else.

contain.definition: If x contains y, y is in x.
contain.sentence: Did the envelope contain a letter?

contemporary.definition: If something is contemporary it is related to this time (now). Technically, this is an incorrect usage; better is to use "modern", "now" or "present-day".
contemporary.sentence: The artist has a great knowledge of the sources of historical and contemporary art.

content.definition: The contents of a container, such as a bag, a file, a book etc., are the things that are in it.
content.sentence: The students were generally happy with the course content and the instructor.

contest.definition: A contest is where people do a quiz or play a game to win a prize.
contest.sentence: He took part in the contest as he wanted to win the first prize.

context.definition: Something's context is the situation that it happens in.
context.sentence: The actions of a business cannot be fully understood except in the context of a particular organisation.

continue.definition: If something continues, it does not stop.

continuous.definition: Something that is continuous happens without stopping.

contract.definition: A contract is a legal agreement to trade goods, services and/or property. It's usually written down.
contract.sentence: If you would just sign this contract, the car will be yours.

contrast.definition: Contrasts are the differences you find when you compare something or someone.
contrast.sentence: Married life is a sharp contrast to the life of a single person.

contribute.definition: If x contributes to y, x is one of a number of things that together make or cause y.
contribute.sentence: Are you able to contribute an hour a week to help us out?

contribution.definition: A contribution is something that you give or add.
contribution.sentence: Technology to reduce pollution could make a significant contribution to the solution.

control.definition: If you have control over someone or something, you can make it do what you want.
control.sentence: He should try to take control and tell the other handlers what to do.

controversial.definition: Something that is causing debate, causing talk and discussion.
controversial.sentence: The latest book about UFOs has been very controversial.

convention.definition: A convention is a large meeting of a specific group or for a specific purpose.
convention.sentence: There's a doctor's convention in town this week and all the hotels are full.

conventional.definition: Something that is conventional is what is generally done, believed, or ordinary.
conventional.sentence: The train runs on conventional rails.

conversation.definition: A conversation is when two or more people are talking informally.
conversation.sentence: I had a really interesting conversation at work about how to improve things.

convert.definition: If you convert something, you change it so that it has a different function or form.
convert.sentence: They wanted to convert the room into a study.

convince.definition: To make someone believe, or feel sure about something.
convince.sentence: We have to convince her that the world is a sphere.

cook.definition: To bake or boil, to prepare food.

cool.definition: If something is cool, its temperature is between warm and cold.
cool.sentence: It's hard to keep the house nice and cool on a hot summer's day.

cooperation.definition: Cooperation is the act of working together to achieve a shared goal.
cooperation.sentence: The project succeeded because of the cooperation between the two teams.

cope.definition: If you cope with a problem, you do things so that the problem does not stop you.
cope.sentence: She went to a special school and learned the skills needed to cope with her learning differences.

copy.definition: A copy of something looks or acts like it.
copy.sentence: They took the diamond and replaced it with a cheap copy.

core.definition: The core is the centre part of something.
core.sentence: I bit into the apple core and spit out the seeds.

corner.definition: A corner is the place where two lines or edges meet.
corner.sentence: They live on the corner of Main Street and Dundas.

corporate.definition: Corporate finance, planning, management, etc. is related to business or a company.
corporate.sentence: We have accounts for both individual and corporate clients.

corporation.definition: A corporation is a large company or a group of companies that work together.
corporation.sentence: The Canadian Broadcasting Corporation is Canada's national radio and TV broadcaster.

correct.definition: Something that is correct has no mistakes.
correct.sentence: When you type, the correct hand position is very important.

correspond.definition: If x corresponds to y, there is a close relationship between x and y.

cost.definition: The cost of something is the price that a person pays for it.
cost.sentence: What is the cost of the car?

cough.definition: If you cough, you quickly blow air out and make a noise because of a feeling in the throat.

could.definition: If you could do something, you were able to do it.
could.sentence: When I was younger, I could run a five-minute mile.

council.definition: A council is a group of people who are chosen or elected to make laws, rules, and decisions.
council.sentence: Town council is considering a road-widening proposal.

counsel.definition: Counsel is the giving or receiving of advice.

count.definition: If you count something, you find how many there are, usually by looking at them one by one.
count.sentence: OK kids, first everyone get on the bus, and then we'll count to see that everyone's here.

counter.definition: A counter is a flat surface to work on, often in a kitchen.
counter.sentence: A counter may be used to stiffen the material around the heel and to give support to the foot.

country.definition: A land that is controlled by a government.
country.sentence: Russia is the largest country in the world.

county.definition: A county is an area of land with a local government, often including a number of towns or cities. It is used differently in different countries.
county.sentence: My grandfather lived his whole life in my home county of Sussex.

couple.definition: A couple is two (2) things that go together.
couple.sentence: Can you lend me a couple of dollars?

course.definition: In school, a course is a class in a specific subject.
course.sentence: The science course was very difficult.

court.definition: A court is where people are tried for crimes.
court.sentence: The bad guy goes to court to stand before the judge.

cousin.definition: Your cousin is the son or daughter of your aunt or uncle.

cover.definition: Something that is covering another thing is on top of (or over) the other thing in a way that stops people from seeing it.
cover.sentence: I cover myself in two blankets at night to stay warm.

coverage.definition: Coverage is the amount something or someone is covered.
coverage.sentence: The dictionary's coverage of standard English is excellent.

cow.definition: A common farm animal, the female cattle.

crack.definition: When something cracks it breaks along a line, maybe not a straight line. It might break into two pieces, or it might break but the two pieces are still attached.

craft.definition: When you craft an object, it means that you make the object by hand.
craft.sentence: That craftsman is real good, he can craft out a complicated ship out of a block of wood.

crash.definition: A crash is something that happens between things. Something that comes together.
crash.sentence: I saw a horrible crash on my way home. Two cars had hit each other.

crazy.definition: If someone is crazy, they do not think or act normally. A crazy person might do very strange thing or believe things that everyone knows are not true.

cream.definition: Cream is the fatty part of milk.
cream.sentence: Would you like some cream in your coffee?

create.definition: If you create something, you make or invent it. Usually, it's something that nobody has made before.

creation.definition: The act of creating is called creation.
creation.sentence: The creation of a house takes time.

creative.definition: If you are creative you are good at making things that no one has made before. Also, it could mean you are good at thinking of things no one has thought of before.
creative.sentence: The inventor had a very creative idea for a new machine.

creature.definition: A creature is a large animal, especially a created (mythical) nonhuman.

credit.definition: Credit is an agreement to buy something and pay later.
credit.sentence: We bought the new dining room table on credit.

crew.definition: A group of people working together to operate something such as a ship, factory, airplane, etc.

crime.definition: A crime is an act that is against the law and for which you can go to jail.
crime.sentence: New York has a lot of crime.

criminal.definition: Criminal law, charges, investigations, and so forth are ones related to crime.

crisis.definition: A crisis is a situation that has become very bad or dangerous and can have bad changes to security, economic, political, social or environmental issues.
crisis.sentence: This will be president's last trip to the Persian Gulf until the crisis has been resolved.

criteria.definition: The plural form of criterion; more than one (kind of) criterion.
criteria.sentence: One of the criteria for measuring the success of a democracy is the percentage of people that vote in that society .

critical.definition: Something that criticizes or includes criticism.

criticism.sentence: Their marriage received a lot of criticism from their families.

criticize.definition: If you criticize something, you point out its flaws or faults.
criticize.sentence: Those who criticize others often are not perfect, either.

crop.definition: A plant that is grown on a farm.
crop.sentence: The latest crop of fashions is about to hit the stores.

cross.definition: If you cross something, you go from one side of it to the other side.
cross.sentence: Don't cross the street until the light turns green.

crowd.definition: A crowd is a lot of people in one place together.
crowd.sentence: The crowd cheered when the team scored another goal.

crucial.definition: When something is crucial, it is very important. It will make a big difference. You cannot succeed without it.
crucial.sentence: To write a great book, it's crucial to have the person in the book change and develop.

cry.definition: To shed tears; to let water come from your eyes, usually while making a sound, usually when you feel sad.
cry.sentence: He started to cry because he was so upset.

cultural.definition: A cultural background, difference, identity etc. relates or belongs to a particular group of people.
cultural.sentence: Teachers should think about the cultural background of their students.

culture.definition: A culture is a common history, set of beliefs, or way of life within a group of people.
culture.sentence: Rock and roll is a central part of American popular culture.

cup.definition: A cup is deep round container open at the top, normally used to drink out of.
cup.sentence: I'll bring you another cup of tea.

curious.definition: If someone is curious, they ask a lot of questions and want to know new things.

currency.definition: A currency is the money from a particular country.
currency.sentence: A person going abroad can obtain foreign currency notes and travellers' cheques from his own bank.

current.definition: Something that is current is up to date.

currently.definition: If something is happening currently it is happening at this time.
currently.sentence: They are currently trying call home.

curtain.definition: Curtains are pieces of cloth that hang in front of a window, door, or stage.
curtain.sentence: The base of the rock is undercut, permitting walkers to pass behind the curtain of falling water.

curve.definition: A curve is a line that is not straight. It is like part of a circle. It starts in one direction and turns.
curve.sentence: The edge of the flower petal is a beautiful curve.

custom.definition: A custom is an activity that happens traditionally or regularly.
custom.sentence: My mother's custom is to have breakfast in the garden with her newspaper.

customer.definition: A customer is a person who pays money for goods or services.

cut.definition: If you make something shorter or divide it in pieces, you cut it.
cut.sentence: Jared cut the meat using his knife and fork.

cycle.definition: A cycle is a number of regular things that happen again and again.
cycle.sentence: Right now we are in an upward-moving part of the business cycle.
